claims.text: The initial W38Ta36Cr15V11 alloy is nanocrystalline, uniform, and producible by conventional powder metallurgy.
The proposed intervention is to add 0.5–1.0 at.% Zr during powder synthesis.
Trace Zr addition will cause Zr to segregate from the matrix to grain boundaries.
Zr segregation will produce Zr-enriched nanoscale interfacial layers at grain boundaries.
Zr has a strong chemical affinity for grain-boundary sites in this alloy.
Grain-boundary Zr will act as a getter that traps mobile Cr and V solutes.
Trapping Cr and V at Zr-enriched interfaces will retard nucleation and growth of Cr–V-rich precipitates.
Grain boundaries can act as recombination or annihilation sinks and thereby reduce irradiation-defect concentrations.
The proposed Zr-mediated defect-sink action will keep the nanocrystalline matrix intact under irradiation.
Zr addition will markedly reduce or completely suppress Cr–V-rich precipitates relative to undoped W38Ta36Cr15V11.
The precipitate-suppression effect will remain effective through an irradiation dose of 8 dpa.
The Zr-modified alloy will preserve the low irradiation hardening of the baseline alloy.
The Zr-modified alloy will preserve the baseline alloy's radiation resistance.
Trace Zr addition will preserve practical bulk manufacturability.
Maintaining the irradiation specimen below approximately 700 °C will control Zr diffusion and prevent unwanted phase formation.
Keeping Zr within 0.5–1.0 at.% will avoid Zr-rich secondary phases that would adversely affect properties.
The Zr-modified alloy will have improved post-irradiation fracture toughness relative to the undoped alloy.
Undoped nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 develops Cr–V-rich precipitates near 8 dpa.
Cr–V-rich precipitates in the undoped alloy cause increased hardening and brittleness.
The optimal Zr concentration and Zr segregation kinetics under the proposed irradiation conditions are not known precisely.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome characterize the undoped alloy as having low hardening that should be preserved, whereas the baseline states that its irradiation-induced precipitates produce increased hardening and brittleness. No qualification reconciles negligible or low hardening with the asserted increase.
